overview:
Zintro is a pioneer of the self-service expert network model, founded in 2007 by serial entrepreneur Stuart Lewtan in Boston. Lewtan conceived Zintro while serving as an executive-in-residence at a prominent Boston VC/PE firm, where he found existing expert networks overpriced and cumbersome. His solution: a marketplace where clients could post project briefs, receive expert responses within hours, and engage directly — with complete price transparency.

Zintro's core innovation is its dual service model. Clients can use the platform on a fully self-service basis (posting projects, reviewing expert responses, scheduling calls independently) or opt for full-service support comparable to GLG or AlphaSights, but at 30-75% lower cost. The company achieves this by maintaining remote operations teams in the Philippines and India alongside its Boston headquarters.

With 1M+ expert profiles and 500+ active clients ranging from startups to Global 1000 enterprises, Zintro has carved out a sustainable niche as the cost-effective, transparent alternative to premium expert networks. The company generates an estimated ~$7.1M in annual revenue and has operated profitably without major venture capital dependency.

history.narrative:
Stuart Lewtan is a serial entrepreneur with a track record of successful technology ventures. Before Zintro, he founded Lewtan Technologies, a 100+ person company serving 400+ institutional clients in the asset-backed securities industry, which was acquired by DMG Information in 2004 (later sold to Moody's in 2015). He also co-founded MicroE Systems (precision motion control, acquired by GSI Group) and Axsun Technologies (MEMS-based optical engines for telecom and medical imaging).

Lewtan conceived Zintro around 2007 while serving as an executive-in-residence at a prominent Boston VC/PE firm, where he experienced firsthand the high costs and friction of traditional expert networks. He built Zintro as a fully self-service platform with no human intermediation. Over time, client demand led to the addition of full-service capabilities, creating the dual model that defines Zintro today.

servicesDetailed.name: Self-Service Marketplace
servicesDetailed.description: Clients post project briefs to the platform; Zintro's algorithm anonymously matches them to relevant experts. Typically 5-12 experts respond within hours to a few days. Clients review profiles, select experts, and schedule calls independently. Complete price transparency with itemized expert fees and Zintro margins.

servicesDetailed.name: Full-Service Expert Calls
servicesDetailed.description: Traditional expert network service where Zintro's fulfillment team handles recruiting, screening, compliance, scheduling, transcription, and expert payment — comparable to GLG or AlphaSights but at 30-75% lower cost.

servicesDetailed.name: Surveys & Quantitative Research
servicesDetailed.description: Participant recruitment from the 1M+ expert database for quantitative studies and structured survey research.

servicesDetailed.name: AI-Moderated Interviews
servicesDetailed.description: Supporting clients using AI-driven interview moderation. Zintro reports that 82% of surveyed participants preferred AI-moderated over live interviews.

servicesDetailed.name: Custom Expert Recruiting
servicesDetailed.description: Tracking down niche experts outside the existing network for specialized requirements that the 1M+ database cannot fulfill.

servicesDetailed.name: Recruiting & Talent Placement
servicesDetailed.description: Facilitating full-time and part-time placements through the expert network, charging a 15% fee on first-year compensation.

aiPlatform.narrative: Zintro's proprietary matching algorithm understands semantic relationships between keywords — for example, a search for 'securitization specialists' automatically surfaces experts with 'MBS' or 'structured finance' in their profiles. Results are distilled into a single relevance coefficient for force-ranking experts. The algorithm can identify non-obvious expert matches that human recruiters might miss due to search habit bias, a capability Zintro calls 'alpha-generating discovery.' All initial client-expert interactions are anonymous until both parties agree to engage.

The self-service model places more compliance responsibility on the client, while the full-service option includes screening, NDA management, and conflict checks handled by Zintro's team.

clientFit.narrative: Zintro is ideal for cost-conscious organizations that value price transparency and want control over their expert engagement process. The self-service model appeals to teams comfortable managing their own research, while the full-service option serves those who want traditional expert network support at lower cost. Premium institutional clients requiring the deepest compliance infrastructure may prefer established players.
